title: Counting Arrays
statementMd:
VegiCat gives you two integers n and m. Consider integer arrays a1,a2,…,an such that

a1=0,0≤ai+1−ai≤1(1≤i<n).

Let si=a1+a2+…+ai be the prefix sums of a. VegiCat also tells you the prefix sums at m positions; that is, you are given m constraints of the form spj=vj (1≤j≤m).

Count the number of arrays satisfying all constraints, modulo 998244353. If no array satisfies all the constraints, the answer is 0.

## Input

The first line contains an integer T (1≤T≤104), the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

Each test case is given as follows:

The first line contains two integers n and m (1≤n≤100, 0≤m≤n), the length of the array and the number of prefix sum constraints, respectively.

The j-th of the next m lines contains two integers pj and vj (1≤pj≤n, 0≤vj≤109). This describes a constraint: the sum of the first pj elements of the array must equal vj.

The positions pj are given in strictly increasing order.

## Output

For each test case, output an integer — the number of valid arrays modulo 998244353.

## Note

Without any prefix constraints there are exactly 2n−1 such arrays, because each of the n−1 adjacent differences may independently be 0 or 1.

In the second test case, the only array with s3=1 is (0,0,1).

In the third test case, s2=0 forces a2=0, after which a3 may be 0 or 1.

In the fourth test case, the arrays are (0,1,1,1) and (0,0,1,2).

In the fifth test case, the arrays with s5=4 are (0,0,1,1,2) and (0,1,1,1,1).

In the sixth test case, s2=0 forces a1=a2=0, so s5≤6. The constraint s5=10 is impossible.
